applies_why: The judge text does not use a single verse's failure to state a link or its contrary as a ground; it cites a dropped limb and the absence of a live contradictor.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED: one reading bars only silence-based grounds; the other bars any underdetermination involving one verse. I adopted the first.
why: The judge's stated ground is the defender's dropped limb leaving no live contradictor, not that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary, so K-S2 is not violated.
